statement: The labelled cyclic 7-root system has exactly 924 distinct complex solutions, all of multiplicity one.

answer.multiplicity: Every solution has intersection multiplicity one.

source.location: Introduction, printed p.2: table of γ(n) and paragraph stating multiplicity one for p=2,3,5,7; Theorem 6.4, printed p.23

origin.inheritance_basis: Theorem 6.4 gives binomial(2*7-2,7-1)=924 with multiplicity; the introduction separately states all roots are simple for p=2,3,5,7.

notes:
Haagerup explicitly recalls simplicity for these small primes. Simplicity for arbitrary prime length is not asserted.

The earlier924-root enumeration is Backelin–Fröberg (1991), as credited in Haagerup’s introduction; Haagerup supplies the inspected recap, including simplicity.

Jörgen Backelin; Ralf Fröberg, How we proved that there are exactly 924 cyclic 7-roots (1991, article ID backelin_froberg_1991_cyclic7). Historical attribution recorded by the cited supporting article. No separately inspected result locator in this earlier article was recorded for this result.
